title: Knowledge Check 3 - Lessons 11-15
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 11-15 - FlexCards. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A FlexCard must display a flat list of the five most recent cases for the current account, refreshing whenever the record changes. Which data source is the most efficient choice?
options: Static JSON
Turbo Extract
Standard Extract
Integration Procedure
questions.explanation: A Turbo Extract runs a single SOQL query against the context record and returns a flat result set, which is exactly the shape and refresh behavior this card needs, and it is the fastest live-data path. Static JSON cannot reflect live record data. A standard Extract or Integration Procedure adds orchestration the card does not need for a single flat list.

questions.question: A FlexCard must render an account with its contacts and its open opportunities as separate nested collections, plus a computed total. Which data source is required?
options: Static JSON
Turbo Extract
Standard Extract
Integration Procedure
questions.explanation: Nested collections and a computed value require orchestration: an Integration Procedure can loop, aggregate, and assemble a nested JSON payload that the card binds to. Turbo Extract and standard Extract both return flat rows and cannot produce the nested shape. Static JSON cannot reflect live data.

questions.question: A consultant is choosing a data source for a card that only ever shows fixed option labels that never change. What is the correct choice and why?
options: Turbo Extract, because it is the fastest live source
Static JSON, because the data never changes and needs no server round trip
Integration Procedure, because it is the most flexible
Standard Extract, because it can run multiple queries
questions.explanation: Static JSON is embedded in the card definition and needs no server round trip, which is ideal for fixed labels and option lists that never change. Turbo Extract, standard Extract, and Integration Procedure all fetch live data, which is unnecessary and adds latency for data that is constant.

questions.question: A FlexCard shows reference data that never changes and is collapsed by default. Which setup configuration is most efficient?
options: Re-fetch on every context change and load the full payload on render
Load once and defer the heavy fetch until the card is expanded
Re-fetch on a short timer so the data stays current
Disable the data source entirely and rely on static JSON
questions.explanation: Static reference data should load once, and a collapsed card should not pay for a heavy payload until it is expanded, so deferring the fetch is the efficient choice. Re-fetching on context change or on a timer adds needless queries for data that never changes. Disabling the source would break the card if it needs any data at all.

questions.question: A card is showing stale data after a user edits the underlying record. What is the most likely cause?
options: The data source query is wrong
The card is not set to re-fetch when the context record changes
The card is expanded by default
The card has no actions configured
questions.explanation: Stale data after a record edit points to the refresh behavior: the card is not re-fetching when the context record changes. A wrong query would show wrong data, not stale data. The expanded state and the presence of actions do not control data freshness.

questions.question: A consultant is auditing a card that fetches far too often and slows the page. Which setup property should they check first?
options: The load and refresh behavior
The element styling
The action wiring
The card title
questions.explanation: Fetch frequency is governed by the load and refresh behavior in the setup properties, so that is the first place to look. Element styling, action wiring, and the title do not control how often the card fetches data.

questions.question: A FlexCard must show an account's key fields, a table of its contacts, and a chart of opportunities by stage. How should the data be assembled?
options: Three independent Turbo Extracts bound to three elements
An Integration Procedure that merges the account, contacts, and aggregated opportunity data into one payload
Static JSON for all three sections
A single standard Extract returning one flat list
questions.explanation: The card needs multiple data shapes, including a nested collection and an aggregated series, so an Integration Procedure should assemble them into one payload the card binds to. Independent Turbo Extracts would not produce the nested and aggregated shapes cleanly. Static JSON cannot reflect live data, and a single flat Extract cannot produce the required structure.

questions.question: Which element is the correct choice for showing a collection of related records on a FlexCard?
options: A text element
A data table
A single input
A menu
questions.explanation: A collection of related records is tabular data, so a data table is the correct element. A text element shows a single value, an input captures one value, and a menu selects from discrete options; none of them present a collection clearly.

questions.question: A consultant is designing a card and wants the user to understand what record it is about before seeing detail. What is the correct layout principle?
options: Lead with the chart so the data is prominent
Lead with identity, then key facts, then supporting detail, then actions
Put all data in one data table
Place the actions at the top
questions.explanation: A logical top-to-bottom order leads with identity so the user knows what the card is about, then key facts, then supporting detail, then actions. Leading with a chart before context forces the user to hunt for what the record is. One data table cannot hold mixed data types, and actions belong after the content they act on.

questions.question: A service agent resolves cases and a manager reviews case trends. Both will see a case FlexCard. What is the correct design approach?
options: Show the same full set of fields and actions to both roles
Design for the agent's task and use conditional rendering to adapt the card for the manager's read-only view
Remove all actions so neither role can act
Show only the manager's aggregate data to both
questions.explanation: The card should be designed around the primary role's task, then adapted for other roles with conditional rendering, so the agent gets the fields and actions to resolve cases and the manager gets a read-only view. Showing the same full set to both buries what each needs. Removing all actions breaks the agent's workflow, and showing only aggregates breaks the agent's task.

questions.question: What is the primary driver of which data a FlexCard should display?
options: The full set of fields on the object
The role's task and the context where the user acts
The number of elements available
The size of the data source
questions.explanation: Role and context drive the design: the card should show the data the user needs to complete their task in the moment they act. The full field set, the element count, and the source size are not the drivers; they are constraints the design works within.

questions.question: A card for a sales rep shows every opportunity field and every possible action. What is the main problem with this design?
options: The data source is too small
The card lacks a chart
The card buries the data and actions that matter under noise
The card is read-only
questions.explanation: Showing every field and action buries the data and actions that matter, forcing the rep to filter mentally. The problem is not the source size, the absence of a chart, or read-only status; it is the lack of role-based focus and clarity.

questions.question: A user clicks a button on a FlexCard and must complete a multi-step guided process to resolve a case. Which action type should be used?
options: A link to a URL
A modal with a small form
Launching an OmniScript
A static text element
questions.explanation: A multi-step guided process is exactly what an OmniScript is for, so the action should launch the OmniScript and pass the context record. A link navigates away without the guided flow, a modal is for a short in-context interaction, and a text element is not an action.

questions.question: A user needs to enter a single short value without leaving the current card. Which action is the best fit?
options: A link to a record page
A modal that opens in context
Launching a full OmniScript
Calling an Integration Procedure with no UI
questions.explanation: A short, focused capture that should not interrupt the user's flow is best handled by a modal that opens in context. A link navigates away, a full OmniScript is overkill for one value, and an IP with no UI gives the user no way to enter the value.

questions.question: A user's click should run a server-side calculation and the card should then show the updated result. Which action should be used?
options: A link to an external site
A modal
Calling an Integration Procedure, then refreshing the card
A child FlexCard with no data
questions.explanation: Running a server-side operation and reflecting the result is the job of an Integration Procedure action, followed by a card refresh to show the new state. A link navigates away, a modal is for capture, and a child FlexCard without data does not run the calculation.
